top_issues.reason: Security hardening: a relative cache-dir set in the project config leads to pickle.load on files that whoever wrote the repo controls, so running Black on such a checkout can execute arbitrary code.
Black silently skips files git tracks when a nested .gitignore negation re-includes them, so --check passes in CI anyway; it is confirmed in real repos and a small fix has been proposed.
Planning issue that decides which preview features become part of the 2027 stable style; it ties together many preview-style feedback issues.
Target versions are inferred wrongly from compatible-release requires-python constraints (~=3.11.0 gives py311 through py315); PRs are already open, and the related older case is in #3581.
Black hangs indefinitely on files with very long nested dicts, a performance/denial-of-service bug that also connects to the memory work in #5216.

records.judge_reason: The report closely matches the labelled structure. Comments/pragmas, line splitting, file discovery/config, performance and string processing/preview all map well onto labelled themes. Integrations and packaging are merged into one theme, which is defensible. A few issues are misplaced. #4058 (parenthesis around walrus) is a style issue but sits under Packaging/CI. #3769 (--diff line numbers) is an output issue but sits under file discovery. #4276 (docstring indentation) and #3504 (multiline string spacing) are under Comments rather than style. #5658 is under preview, which is defensible. #5546 and #4438 are moved into performance/security, which is reasonable. Overall these are mostly the labelled groupings with a handful of misplacements.

duplicates.reason: Both come from the eager --config callback running before src_files is parsed, so config discovery falls back to the CWD. A maintainer confirmed this in 2096, which is already labelled duplicate.
In both, stale pins in an existing requirements.txt conflict with a changed .in requirement, and pip-compile errors out instead of dropping the outdated pin.

top_issues.reason: Regression in 7.6.1: the JSON API URL lost /pypi/, so --generate-hashes silently downloads every file (GBs). It affects Dependabot, and a one-line fix is known.
Confirmed regression: pip-compile hangs on named-pipe input because the input is read twice.
After leaving Jazzband the project has no security reporting policy. This is needed for handling vulnerabilities.
Long-standing config discovery bug: config files next to the input files are ignored and a spurious --config shows up in the header. A duplicate (2096) has been filed and a fix exists.
Changing a pinned version in the .in file makes pip-compile fail with ResolutionImpossible unless --upgrade is passed. Several users are affected, and 1997 is a duplicate.

records.judge_reason: The report matches several labelled themes well: Resolver, Hashes/caching, and pip-sync, with a few misplacements. #2047 (an index issue) is placed under resolver. #2080 (a PEP 740 issue) is placed under hashes, which is arguably defensible. #2002 (a resolver/extras issue) is placed under packaging. #2173 and #2172 (index/hermetic issues) are placed under packaging/CI. It merges two labelled themes, config/CLI and output/header, into one large theme, and moves the pip-sync config issues (#2093, #2187) into it. It also creates a separate 'error handling' theme that pulls issues from the config, output and resolver themes. That theme is somewhat coherent, but it slices across topics. The biggest problem is the final theme, which lumps packaging standards (PEPs) together with CI, docs and maintenance. These are distinct topics, so it is a mixed grab-bag. Several issues are missing, for example #1873, #1831, #2025, #2182, #2160, #2151, #1850 and #1804. Overall some themes match closely, but there are merged and mixed themes and misplacements.

duplicates.reason: Both ask for surnames and personal names to get their correct reading, and the maintainer points 297 to 120.

top_issues.reason: In heteronym mode, many common characters (受, 惊, 餐) get readings that look like errors. The bug is still there in 0.55.0 and affects a lot of output.
Clear data error: phrases_dict marks 乡长 as xiāng cháng instead of xiāng zhǎng. It is easy to fix.

Common phrases get the wrong reading because a word that overlaps them is matched first (试着重复 is split around 着重), which hurts accuracy in normal use.
栅 in technical terms (浮栅, 栅极) should be read shān. The fix is a simple data change for a whole set of words.

records.judge_reason: The report's five themes broadly follow the labelled structure, with some reshuffling. Wrong readings are split into single characters versus phrases and polyphone disambiguation. That split is defensible and fairly coherent, and it moves #375, #369 and #358 into the phrase group. Tones and sandhi matches well and reasonably adds erhua (#144). Problems: #221 is listed twice, in both the single-character theme and the tones theme. The data-sources group is dissolved: #43 and #342 go into phrase readings, which is plausible, and #307 and #184 go into a broad 'New API, output and data features' bucket. That bucket also absorbs romanisation and format bugs such as #365 and #355, mixing bug reports with feature requests. The C/C++ ports theme is narrow but coherent. Overall it is mostly coherent, with a few misplacements, one duplicate and one broader catch-all theme.

themes.name: Wrong readings for specific characters or phrases

duplicates.reason: Both ask for special handling of polyphonic surnames (for example 查 read as zhā), and the maintainer points #297 to #120.
Both report that neutral-tone words such as 妈妈 and 爸爸 get the full dictionary tone instead of a neutral tone, and both are answered with the load_phrases_dict workaround.
Both complain that single characters carry archaic or rare readings that are not in modern dictionaries, and the maintainer refers #293 to #263.
Both report that heteronym=True returns readings like dào for 受 or tái and xióng for 能, which come from the same Hanyu Da Zidian data source.
Both ask whether there is a native C or C++ version of the library, and the answer to both is no.

top_issues.reason: A wrong entry in phrases_dict.json for the common word 乡长 (it gives cháng instead of zhǎng) gives wrong output in default use. It is easy to fix.
栅 in technical terms such as 浮栅 is read zhà instead of shān. This is a clear data fix that affects common technical vocabulary.
Many common characters show readings that do not belong to them when heteronym=True. Users still report it in 0.55.0, and the root cause is shared with #293 and #263.
Common neutral-tone words (早上, 妈妈, 东西) get full tones. This affects learners widely, and the maintainer plans a design fix.
There is no special handling for polyphonic surnames. The request keeps coming back (#297 asks again), and #297 lists the surname readings needed.

records.judge_reason: The report's themes are mostly coherent. The tone theme matches the labelled one, with #144 (erhua) added as a reasonable extra. The API/output features theme is close to the labelled romanisation/output theme, though it also takes in #362, #307 and #184. Splitting off names (#120, #297) and C/C++ ports (#233, #212) is defensible. The weak spot is how the dictionary readings are divided. The first theme mixes wrong single readings with segmentation and heteronym problems (#344, #302, #286, #249), so it blurs the labelled heteronyms/segmentation theme. The 'rare readings' theme puts heteronym-data complaints (#263, #293, #321) together with data-source and project items (#43, #342, #133), which is a looser mix. #284 is misplaced. Overall it mostly holds up, but with several misplacements and overlap between the two reading-error themes.
